paragraphs: A student of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, as in [Taanit 18a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.18a.12), where Bali transmits a ruling from him, and Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to him, “I will explain it to you” ([Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Taanit.18a.12.1) explains: Bali is a sage’s name). In [Berakhot 25b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.25b.23), Bali reports a teaching in the name of Rav Yaakov, the son of Shmuel’s daughter. In [Shabbat 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.17b.4), Bali transmits a teaching in the name of Avimi Sanvata’ah; [Avodah Zarah 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.36a.8) reads Avimi Nota’ah.[^2]

notes.text: תלמדו is read as תלמידו, “his student.”

In [Taanit 18a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.18a.12), Bali reports that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba taught the ruling in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. [Avodah Zarah 36a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.36a.8) adds Rav at the end of its chain. The parallel [Seder HaDorot entry on Bali](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=660&lang=en) records both forms of the Avimi attribution.
